svg.text: claudia — The first administrator needs a setup code (SEC-12), proposed
Only someone who can read the server's own log (or its state folder) can name the first administrator. FirstAdminSetup.vue gets one field; AdminLogin.vue and the settings pages
do not change. Recommended variant B: every server asks for the code, whatever address it listens on; the desktop apps hand it over themselves, so a person on their own computer types nothing.
The server says the code where only its operator looks
At every start with no administrator: in the banner, in the log, and in a file of the state folder. Never over HTTP.

Name yourself as this server's administrator
claudia.example.org can be reached from other computers. To show that you
run it, give the setup code from the server's log, then a name and a password
for yourself. You will use them to sign in here from now on.
In the server's log where it started, or in
admin/setup-code in its state folder. A restart
of the server makes a new code.
If every administrator is ever locked out, whoever runs the server starts it once
with --reset-administrators; it then asks for a first administrator with a new code.

Desktop app: one person on their own computer types nothing
The Linux, Windows and macOS apps start the server on 127.0.0.1. They read
the code from its state folder and give it to their own page.
Name yourself as this server's administrator
This computer's own server isn't reachable from other computers, so this isn't required — but
set a name and password now if you'd like to manage its settings (AI model, fonts, typesetting).
…password, confirm password as in 2. No setup code field: the app gave the code.
Who has to give a code
A: as SEC-12 proposes (only when --host is not loopback).
Desktop app (127.0.0.1, started by the app)
yes, the link in the terminal
On 127.0.0.1 behind a proxy on the same machine
Another account on the same computer
"Exposed" today means only that --host is not a loopback address. A server on 127.0.0.1 behind
nginx or Caddy on the same machine is reachable from everywhere and still counts as not exposed,
and every account on a shared computer (a school's, a terminal server) reaches 127.0.0.1.
An administrator can name any program as xelatex (SEC-16), so taking over a server means
running programs as the account that runs it.
Locked out, or deploying: two start options
--reset-administrators removes the administrators only; settings, documents and fonts stay.
--admin NAME with --admin-password-file FILE names the first one at start (the demo, Docker).
administrators reset: anna, ben removed (kept aside as
no administrator yet: name one with this setup code, which works until
one is named or the server stops
--admin never changes an administrator who exists: with one already there it says so and
does nothing. With --reset-administrators it names the new first one in the same start.
